hook_text: Heat 50 g of chalk and only 28 g of solid can ever come out. Chemistry knew before the oven did.
clip_script: Fifty grams of calcium carbonate goes into the heat. How much calcium oxide can possibly come out? The equation is a recipe written in moles, so make the three moves. Move one: 50 grams at 100 grams per mole is half a mole. Move two: the ratio is one to one — half a mole of carbonate, half a mole of oxide. Move three: half a mole at 56 grams per mole is 28 grams. That is the ceiling — the atoms cannot build more. And the missing 22 grams? Not lost. Half a mole of carbon dioxide, 44 grams per mole, floated away as gas. Add it back: 28 plus 22 is exactly 50. Every atom accounted for.
visual_style: A bag labelled 50 g crosses a bridge over the equation; it splits into a 28 g solid block and a 22 g gas cloud whose masses snap together to rebuild the 50.
pacing: Bold question, three brisk moves, gas-cloud reveal, snap-shut mass balance.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and judge the learner's 25,2 grams with a percentage yield.
